title: Contains Duplicate
oneLinerQuestion: Check if any value appears at least twice in an integer array.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Contains Duplicate problem asks whether any value appears at least twice in an integer array. A brute-force pairwise comparison requires O(N^2) time, while sorting the array reduces this to O(N log N) time at the expense of modifying the input or paying for extra space. By leveraging a Hash Set, we can achieve optimal O(N) linear time: a Hash Set provides amortized O(1) membership checks and insertions. As we stream through the array, each element is queried against the set of previously seen numbers; the moment an element is already present, we have detected a duplicate and can terminate early without inspecting the remainder of the array.

- Step 1: Base Case & Edge Checking — If `nums.length <= 1`, the array has zero or one element and cannot possibly contain duplicates, so we immediately return `false`.

- Step 2: Hash Set Initialization — We initialize an empty hash set: `seen = new Set()`. This set will dynamically buffer the unique values encountered during the linear scan.

- Step 3: Linear Array Traversal — We iterate through each element `num` in the array `nums` sequentially from index 0 to `nums.length - 1`.

- Step 4: Membership Lookup & Early Exit — For the current element, we query the set: `if (seen.has(num))`. If the lookup evaluates to `true`, `num` has occurred at an earlier position in the array, confirming a duplicate; we immediately return `true`.

- Step 5: Recording Unseen Elements — If `num` is not in the set, we insert it: `seen.add(num)`. The loop then proceeds to the next element.

- Step 6: Loop Completion & Final Return — If the entire array is traversed without triggering an early return, every element in `nums` is distinct. We return `false`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) where N is the length of `nums`, as array traversal takes N iterations with amortized O(1) set operations per element. Space Complexity: O(N) auxiliary space in the worst case where all elements are unique, requiring the hash set to store all N integers.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION containsDuplicate(nums):
    seen = EMPTY_SET()
    FOR n IN nums DO:
        IF n IN seen THEN RETURN True
        ADD n TO seen
    END FOR
    RETURN False
END FUNCTION
codeLines: IF n IN seen THEN RETURN True

steps.narration: Line 2: Initialize empty hash set seen = {}.
Line 4: i = 0, n = nums[0] = 1. Check if 1 is in seen: False.
Line 5: Add 1 to seen set -> seen = {1}.
Line 4: i = 1, n = nums[1] = 2. Check if 2 is in seen: False.
Line 5: Add 2 to seen set -> seen = {1, 2}.
Line 4: i = 2, n = nums[2] = 3. Check if 3 is in seen: False.
Line 5: Add 3 to seen set -> seen = {1, 2, 3}.
Line 4: i = 3, n = nums[3] = 1. Check if 1 is in seen: 1 is ALREADY in seen! Duplicate found.
Line 4: Duplicate detected! Early exit, RETURN True.

output.detail: Element 1 appears multiple times. Verified in O(n) time.
